question: How many EU member states will the AI Act National Implementation tracker classify as having clear market surveillance and notifying authorities on January 1, 2027?

calls.reasoning: The FLI tracker (last updated 17 June 2026) currently lists 9 'Clear' states. Since then Germany (KI-MIG enacted 29 July 2026), Poland (law in force 11 Aug 2026) and Greece (Law 5321/2026, July 2026) have enacted designations, so any update would likely push the count to about 12, maybe 13-14. Spain's bill lapsed on 6 Oct 2026. The key uncertainty is whether the tracker is updated before Metaculus checks it on or after Jan 1, 2027. It has been static for about 5 months; I estimate a 30-40% chance of an update, so the status quo of 9 dominates. No human market was found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- FLI tracker (artificialintelligenceact.eu/national-implementation-plans), fetched 2026-11-18: 'Last update: 17 June 2026'. Text says 9 Member States have designated both MSA and notifying authorities. Clear: Cyprus, Denmark, Finland, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Lithuania, Malta, Slovenia. Partial: Czechia, France, Germany, Latvia, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Spain, Sweden. Unclear: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Estonia, Greece.
- The tracker snapshot predates later events: Germany is shown as a draft (cabinet Feb 2026); Poland as passed by the lower house on 11 June 2026, awaiting the Senate.
- agentliability.eu tracker (2026): Germany's KI-MIG enacted 29 July 2026 (Bundesnetzagentur as MSA and notifying authority); Poland's law published 27 July 2026, in force 11 Aug 2026 (KRiBSI as MSA); Ireland's Regulation of AI Act 2026 signed 21 July 2026 (Ireland already Clear on FLI).
- Greece: Law 5321/2026 enacted July 2026. Hellenic DPA is the principal MSA and EETT the notifying authority (Bernitsas, Licentium). FLI currently lists Greece as Unclear.
- Spain: organic AI law bill (approved by cabinet 26 May 2026) lapsed when the Cortes were dissolved on 6 Oct 2026 (imiel.dev, others). AESIA operates but has no new statute.
- Luxembourg: bill 8476 still in committee as of July 2026. Netherlands: draft April 2026. France, Sweden, Austria, Belgium, etc.: no enacted law found as of mid-2026.
- Italy: Legislative Decree 179 of 7 Oct 2026 designates ACN/AgID (Italy already Clear).
- Resolution: resolves off the FLI tracker's 'National Competent Authorities' column as Metaculus sees it on or after 2027-01-01, not off actual legal status. If the page is not updated, it remains at the 17 June snapshot.
- Event window: the tracker state when checked on or after 2027-01-01; as of 2026-11-18, about 6 weeks remain for any tracker update.
- Searched for but did not find: the tracker's historical update cadence/changelog; any announcement of a forthcoming update; enacted laws for Czechia, Portugal, Netherlands, Luxembourg after July 2026.
- Market check: none found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.reference_class: Static web trackers maintained by think tanks: chance of an update within ~6 weeks after a 5-month gap, combined with the count of states that have enacted laws since the last snapshot

calls.reconciliation: Factual premises were consistent across runs. I re-fetched the tracker: the 'Last update: 17 June 2026' stamp and the text count of 9 Clear/12 partial/6 unclear are confirmed. The fetch's table rendering put Spain and Sweden in the Clear column, but that contradicts the page's own count of 9 and all three runs, so I treat it as a parse error. No update history is visible (check came back empty). The remaining disputes are judgment: P(update) of 30-45%, where I take ~38% with no evidence to break the tie; and the conditional count. Greece's July 2026 law (Run 1) plus Germany and Poland support ~12 as the modal outcome if updated, so I weight 12-13 above 10-11. Reference class is my own framing, close to Run 1's.
